text_blocks.snippet: Hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) in adults is usually a mild, self-limiting illness that resolves on its own within 7 to 10 days. Treatment is primarily focused on symptom relief, as there is no specific antiviral medication for HFMD.
snippet_highlighted_words: Treatment is primarily focused on symptom relief, as there is no specific antiviral medication for HFMD

list.snippet: Pain and Fever: Over-the-counter pain relievers like acetaminophen (Tylenol) or ibuprofen (Advil) can help reduce fever and alleviate pain.
Mouth Sores:
Avoid spicy, salty, or acidic foods and drinks that can irritate sores.
Sip cold beverages, suck on ice cubes or popsicles, and eat cold foods like ice cream.
Gargle with warm salt water (for adults who can avoid swallowing) to soothe throat discomfort.
Skin Rash: Calamine lotion can help relieve itching associated with the rash.
Stay Hydrated: Drink plenty of fluids to prevent dehydration, especially if mouth sores make swallowing difficult.
Rest: Get adequate rest to help your body recover.
Hygiene: Practice good hygiene, including frequent handwashing, to prevent spreading the virus to others.
Avoid Close Contact: Stay away from others who have HFMD to minimize the risk of transmission.
Seek Medical Advice: Contact a healthcare professional if you experience severe symptoms, such as high fever, severe dehydration, or complications like neck pain or convulsions.
Fever that is not responding to over-the-counter medications.
Signs of dehydration (dry skin, decreased urination, irritability).
Severe pain or difficulty swallowing.
Neck pain or pain in arms and legs.
Convulsions.

text_blocks.snippet: Note: While most adults experience mild symptoms, some may have atypical or severe cases. In such instances, a doctor may recommend further evaluation and management.

text_blocks.snippet: Hand, foot, and mouth disease (HFMD) is typically thought of as a childhood illness, but adults can also contract it. While generally not serious in adults, it's important to be aware of the symptoms and potential complications.

list.snippet: Fever: A common symptom, often accompanied by flu-like symptoms.
Sore Throat: Painful sores can develop in the mouth and throat.
Rash: A rash with small, red spots or bumps, sometimes turning into blisters, may appear on the hands, feet, and sometimes the buttocks.
Mouth Sores: Painful sores in the mouth can make eating and drinking uncomfortable.
Other Symptoms: Adults may also experience general malaise, irritability, and loss of appetite.
HFMD is generally mild and resolves on its own within 7-10 days for most adults.
Complications are rare, but can include dehydration due to mouth pain, nail loss, and in very rare cases, viral meningitis or encephalitis.
Seek medical attention if: You experience severe symptoms like difficulty breathing, persistent high fever, signs of dehydration, or if symptoms worsen.
Supportive Care: There's no specific treatment for HFMD, so treatment focuses on managing symptoms.
Pain Relief: Over-the-counter pain relievers like acetaminophen or ibuprofen can help with fever and sore throat.
Mouth Sores: Topical oral anesthetics, mouthwashes, or sprays can help relieve pain from mouth sores.
Hydration: Drink plenty of fluids to stay hydrated, especially if mouth sores make it difficult to eat or drink.
Avoid Irritants: Avoid spicy or acidic foods that can irritate mouth sores.
Consult your doctor if: You are pregnant or experience severe symptoms or complications.
